tools.name: MidJourney (image/video)
tools.evidence: Named in a 2025 lawsuit filed by Disney and Universal over training data practices.
tools.source_note: Per public reporting, summer 2025 litigation -- not a legal determination

tools.name: Topaz Video AI
tools.evidence: Training data sourcing not independently verified in public reporting.
tools.source_note: Per public reporting as of 2026 -- not a legal determination

tools.name: Runway (Gen-3/Gen-4, general public tool)
tools.evidence: A federal court found Runway helped train and develop Stable Diffusion and was aware the product uses training images in its operation, denying Runway's motion to dismiss related artist infringement claims (Nov 2024). This status covers Runway's general public tools only -- studio-specific custom-trained partnership models (e.g. Lionsgate's private model) are a separate, non-public asset and would need their own registry entry.
tools.source_note: Per public reporting and court filings as of 2026 -- not a legal determination

tools.name: ElevenLabs -- Iconic Voice Marketplace (verified voices)
tools.evidence: Consent-based licensing for specific named voices (e.g. Michael Caine, Matthew McConaughey), formalized through estate/rights infrastructure via CMG Worldwide. Status applies only to voices confirmed on the Iconic Marketplace roster -- verify the specific voice used, not just the vendor.
tools.source_note: Per public reporting as of 2026 -- not a legal determination

tools.name: ElevenLabs -- general voice cloning (non-marketplace)
tools.evidence: Broad, perpetual training-license terms of service drew public controversy in early 2025 (at least one partner platform publicly ended its integration over the terms). Some historical-figure voices are estate-licensed rather than consented to by the individual, a legally distinct category from marketplace-verified voices.
tools.source_note: Per public reporting as of 2026 -- not a legal determination

tools.name: OpenAI Sora
tools.evidence: OpenAI never confirmed or denied training on YouTube video, and third-party testing found Sora could closely mimic identifiable copyrighted content. OpenAI shut down the Sora app/web experience and its major Disney character-licensing partnership collapsed in March 2026; the Sora API is scheduled for shutdown Sept 24, 2026. Included as a worked example of why registry status needs continuous re-checking, not a one-time lookup -- a tool can be cleared-by-partnership one quarter and non-operational the next.
tools.source_note: Per public reporting as of 2026 -- not a legal determination

tools.name: Kling AI
tools.evidence: Named alongside other major video generators in a February 2026 open letter regarding industry-wide 'Disney-style' rights-holder pressure; commercial terms grant users a usage license rather than clear content ownership.
tools.source_note: Per public reporting as of 2026 -- not a legal determination

tools.name: Pika Labs
tools.evidence: Named among video generation platforms facing industry-wide 'Disney-style' rights-holder pressure as of February 2026; no confirmed licensed-training-data claim identified in public reporting.
tools.source_note: Per public reporting as of 2026 -- not a legal determination

tools.name: Suno
tools.evidence: Warner Music settled its copyright suit and struck a licensing partnership (Nov 2025), but Sony Music's case remains active with a summary-judgment hearing scheduled July 2026; independent-artist class actions are also ongoing.
tools.source_note: Per public reporting as of 2026 -- not a legal determination

tools.name: Udio
tools.evidence: Warner and Universal Music both settled and are building licensed platforms with Udio, but Sony Music's copyright suit remains active as of mid-2026.
tools.source_note: Per public reporting as of 2026 -- not a legal determination

tools.name: Metaphysic AI
tools.evidence: Operates on a per-performer consent and licensing model; markets itself around helping actors copyright their own AI likeness rather than training on unlicensed likenesses.
tools.source_note: Per public reporting and company statements as of 2026 -- not a legal determination; still requires production-level confirmation that performer consent was obtained for the specific shot.

tools.name: Flawless AI (TrueSync / DeepEditor)
tools.evidence: Built in collaboration with guilds and unions; per-project data is ring-fenced and never used for general model training, and its Artistic Rights Treasury requires actor review and consent before any AI-assisted change is released.
tools.source_note: Per company statements as of 2026 -- not a legal determination

tools.name: Synthesia
tools.evidence: Platform terms explicitly place the burden of confirming rights, licenses, and permissions for uploaded content on the user; Synthesia does not itself guarantee the source material is cleared.
tools.source_note: Per Synthesia's own published terms as of 2026 -- not a legal determination

tools.name: Getty Images Generative AI
tools.evidence: Trained exclusively on Getty's owned/licensed creative library with model and property releases maintained; outputs are covered by Getty's indemnification.
tools.source_note: Per Getty Images' own model card and public statements as of 2026 -- not a legal determination

tools.name: Shutterstock AI
tools.evidence: Built on Shutterstock's licensed content catalog; the company markets itself as a rights-cleared data and generation partner to major AI firms.
tools.source_note: Per public reporting as of 2026 -- not a legal determination
